decision.rationale: Keep the published residual neutral trehalase rate with the YPD-grown CEN.PK nth1 deletion strain. The matched wild-type rate gives a descriptive denominator for that extract assay, and the double deletion identifies the residual as NTH2-dependent. Chen and colleagues found higher cellular trehalose after NTH2 deletion in every tested background, including the S288C derivative, Simi White and CSM. The increase was smaller than after NTH1 deletion, and the double deletion accumulated the most. Their assay used added trehalase to quantify stored carbohydrate. These observations support a secondary role for Nth2 in trehalose breakdown while leaving its absolute activity and fraction of turnover in each reference or wine background undetermined.

decision.rationale: Record Nth2 as a functional cytosolic neutral trehalase and leave its numerical contribution in the S288C derivative, Simi White and CSM undetermined. Jules et al. measured NTH2-dependent residual hydrolysis in stationary-phase YPD extracts of a CEN.PK113-7D nth1 deletion strain. Its comparison with the untreated wild type is specific to that assay. Chen et al. report that deleting NTH2 raised the intracellular trehalose pool less than deleting NTH1 within each of five backgrounds, with the highest pool in the double deletion. Their assay quantified stored carbohydrate using added trehalase. Even exact pool differences would leave the native Nth2 rate unidentified. The original passages and reviewed table entries settle the catalogue correction. Sources are Jules et al. (2008), Table 2 and enzyme-assay Methods, doi:10.1128/AEM.00557-07, and Chen et al. (2024), Figure 2a and trehalose measurement Methods, doi:10.1093/g3journal/jkae215.
reconsider_when: Comparable Nth2-dependent hydrolysis rates and isogenic wild-type denominators with uncertainty are available in each named background at matched growth and assay conditions.
